title: Acute Heart Failure and Pulmonary Oedema
caseScenario: A 68-year-old with known ventricular dysfunction reports three days of worsening breathlessness, new orthopnoea, and ankle swelling after a respiratory illness. They are tachypnoeic and cannot lie flat. The case asks the learner to assess perfusion and oxygenation, distinguish congestion from competing acute causes, and plan safe escalation.
learningFocus: Congestion, haemodynamic phenotype, precipitating ischaemia/arrhythmia/infection/renal change, response to acute treatment, and transition back to disease-modifying care.
sourceStatus: Draft for clinician and governance review

title: Diabetic Ketoacidosis
caseScenario: A 24-year-old with type 1 diabetes has vomiting, abdominal discomfort, thirst, and deep rapid breathing after several days of illness and difficulty obtaining insulin. The learner must recognise a metabolic emergency, evaluate ketonaemia and acidosis, correct deficits under protocol, and identify the trigger.
learningFocus: Ketone production and high-anion-gap acidosis, volume and electrolyte depletion, precipitating illness or insulin interruption, and safe transition to a sustainable insulin plan.
sourceStatus: Draft for clinician and governance review

title: Hyperosmolar Hyperglycaemic State
caseScenario: A 77-year-old with type 2 diabetes presents after several days of thirst, poor intake, and increasing confusion during a febrile illness. They are markedly dehydrated. The case asks the learner to assess hyperosmolality, distinguish mixed DKA/HHS and other causes of delirium, and plan cautious protocol-led correction.
learningFocus: Severe free-water deficit, hyperosmolality, neurological status, mixed ketoacidosis, precipitating infection/vascular disease, and serial response monitoring.
sourceStatus: Draft for clinician and governance review

title: Severe Hypoglycaemia
caseScenario: A 59-year-old using insulin is found confused after a night shift and missed meal; a family member reports a recent dose increase. The learner must treat immediate neuroglycopenia, protect swallowing safety, watch for recurrence, and identify a preventable medication or access factor.
learningFocus: Immediate glucose correction, safe route based on consciousness, recurrence risk from long-acting agents, medication/renal review, and a prevention plan.
sourceStatus: Draft for clinician and governance review

title: Acute Exacerbation of COPD
caseScenario: A 70-year-old with COPD and prior admissions reports four days of worse dyspnoea, increased sputum, and reduced walking distance. The learner must grade severity, consider infection and cardiopulmonary mimics, select protocol-based support, and reduce the chance of another exacerbation.
learningFocus: Respiratory failure risk, infection and other triggers, hypercapnia, need for ventilatory support, inhaler use, smoking, and prevention after recovery.
sourceStatus: Draft for clinician and governance review

title: Acute Kidney Injury
caseScenario: A 72-year-old with diabetes has poor intake during gastroenteritis and now reports very little urine. Recent results show a rapid creatinine rise after starting an over-the-counter anti-inflammatory medicine. The learner must assess volume and urgent complications, identify pre-renal/intrinsic/post-renal mechanisms, and plan monitoring.
learningFocus: Baseline versus acute change, fluid state, nephrotoxic exposures, obstruction, urine findings, electrolyte complications, and kidney-safe medication review.
sourceStatus: Draft for clinician and governance review

title: Acute Upper Gastrointestinal Bleeding
caseScenario: A 63-year-old taking an anticoagulant has black stools, dizziness, and one episode of haematemesis. They have a history of chronic liver disease. The learner must assess haemodynamic stability and airway risk, prepare for definitive haemostasis, and account for variceal and medication-related risks.
learningFocus: Bleeding source and rate, compensated versus decompensated blood loss, portal hypertension, antithrombotic exposure, and rebleeding prevention.
sourceStatus: Draft for clinician and governance review

title: Acute Pancreatitis
caseScenario: A 46-year-old develops persistent upper abdominal pain radiating to the back with repeated vomiting after a fatty meal. They have gallstones on prior imaging. The learner must establish the diagnosis, assess organ dysfunction, identify biliary obstruction or another cause, and plan complication monitoring.
learningFocus: Diagnostic criteria, severity and organ failure, biliary cause or cholangitis, appropriate imaging timing, nutrition, and recurrence prevention.
sourceStatus: Draft for clinician and governance review

title: Acute Bowel Obstruction
caseScenario: A 74-year-old with prior abdominal surgery has colicky pain, distension, bilious vomiting, and no flatus for a day. The learner must recognise mechanical obstruction, examine for hernia and peritonitis, identify closed-loop/ischaemic features, and obtain early surgical input.
learningFocus: Mechanical versus functional obstruction, transition point, closed-loop and ischaemia risk, fluid sequestration, and cause-specific intervention.
sourceStatus: Draft for clinician and governance review

title: Acute Poisoning and Overdose
caseScenario: A 31-year-old is brought after a possible deliberate ingestion of several unknown tablets; the time and amount are uncertain. The learner must stabilise airway, breathing, and circulation, identify agent and delayed toxicity, consult toxicology, then assess self-harm and safe disposition.
learningFocus: Immediate physiologic threats, agent/formulation/time, co-ingestants, delayed toxicity, appropriate poison-centre consultation, and mental-health safety.
sourceStatus: Draft for clinician and governance review

title: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Longitudinal Care
caseScenario: A 52-year-old with type 2 diabetes has rising HbA1c, albuminuria, and difficulty taking medicines during shift work. They want to reduce kidney and cardiovascular risk without a complex regimen. The learner must build a shared, individualised plan and close screening gaps.
learningFocus: Glycaemic trajectory, cardiovascular/renal risk, hypoglycaemia burden, pregnancy potential when relevant, complications, adherence barriers, and self-management goals.
sourceStatus: Draft for clinician and governance review

title: Heart Failure
caseScenario: A 66-year-old with reduced ejection fraction has exertional limitation and intermittent ankle swelling, but has missed recent reviews because of transport and medicine costs. The learner must reassess phenotype and congestion, individualise therapy, and create a feasible monitoring plan.
learningFocus: Ejection-fraction phenotype, congestion and functional status, therapy tolerance, renal/potassium monitoring, precipitating comorbidity, and the patient’s access barriers.
sourceStatus: Draft for clinician and governance review

title: Chronic Kidney Disease
caseScenario: A 58-year-old with persistent eGFR reduction and albuminuria has diabetes and hypertension but no current symptoms. The learner must confirm chronicity, stage progression risk, assess cause and complications, and discuss renal-protective care and future preferences.
learningFocus: Chronicity, eGFR and albuminuria risk, underlying cause, cardiovascular burden, medication safety, complications, and early planning for advanced disease.
sourceStatus: Draft for clinician and governance review

title: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease
caseScenario: A 69-year-old with chronic cough and a long exposure history has persistent dyspnoea and two exacerbations this year. They use inhalers inconsistently and have not attended rehabilitation. The learner must confirm obstruction, phenotype symptoms, and prevent further decline.
learningFocus: Objective spirometric diagnosis, symptom and exacerbation burden, inhaler technique, tobacco/exposure, comorbidity, rehabilitation and advanced-support needs.
sourceStatus: Draft for clinician and governance review

title: Asthma
caseScenario: A 27-year-old has episodic wheeze and night waking, uses a reliever most days, and avoids exercise after a recent attack. The learner must confirm variable airflow limitation, review inhaled anti-inflammatory care and technique, and provide an action plan.
learningFocus: Objective diagnostic evidence, control and future attack risk, inhaler technique/adherence, triggers, comorbidities, and appropriate escalation for difficult disease.
sourceStatus: Draft for clinician and governance review

title: Ischaemic Heart Disease
caseScenario: A 61-year-old with known coronary artery disease reports exertional pressure when walking uphill but no rest pain. They stopped a preventive medicine because of muscle symptoms. The learner must exclude instability, reassess function, and agree secondary prevention and symptom control.
learningFocus: Stable versus acute symptom pattern, vascular risk, therapy indication and tolerance, function, adherence, cardiac testing/referral, and rehabilitation.
sourceStatus: Draft for clinician and governance review

title: Dyslipidaemia and Atherosclerotic Risk
caseScenario: A 44-year-old with a strong family history has markedly raised LDL cholesterol but no known vascular disease. The learner must estimate absolute risk, consider inherited or secondary causes, and discuss treatment benefits, risks, and family implications.
learningFocus: Absolute cardiovascular risk, family pattern, secondary causes, lipid phenotype, treatment tolerance, pregnancy considerations, and follow-up response.
sourceStatus: Draft for clinician and governance review

title: Obesity and Weight-Related Health
caseScenario: A 39-year-old with weight-related diabetes, snoring, and knee pain seeks help after repeated restrictive diets and weight regain. The learner must ask permission, understand the person’s priorities, treat complications, and offer sustainable choices without stigma.
learningFocus: Weight trajectory and health impact, medication/sleep/mood factors, eating-disorder risk, person-selected goals, stepped treatment, and long-term support.
sourceStatus: Draft for clinician and governance review

title: Osteoarthritis and Chronic Pain
caseScenario: A 71-year-old with knee pain has reduced activity and worries that movement will damage the joint. Analgesics have caused adverse effects. The learner must check for inflammatory or urgent features, support function, and select multimodal long-term care.
learningFocus: Pain mechanism, function and goals, structural versus inflammatory features, analgesic risk, physical activity, mood/sleep, and indications for imaging or referral.
sourceStatus: Draft for clinician and governance review

title: Hypothyroidism
caseScenario: A 43-year-old reports fatigue, constipation, cold sensitivity, and gradual weight change. TSH is abnormal, but they also have iron deficiency and take a supplement that may interfere with thyroid medicine. The learner must confirm the biochemical pattern, assess cause and pregnancy context, and plan monitored replacement rather than attributing every symptom to thyroid disease.
learningFocus: Symptoms and biochemical confirmation, primary versus central cause, pregnancy/medication context, cardiovascular risk, replacement monitoring, and alternative explanations for persistent symptoms.
sourceStatus: Draft for clinician and governance review

title: Childhood Immunisation and Catch-Up
caseScenario: A parent brings a 20-month-old whose immunisation record is incomplete after a move between regions. The learner must establish reliable records, use the current Saudi schedule, assess contraindications and missed-dose rules, and communicate expected reactions and follow-up.
learningFocus: Age- and risk-appropriate schedule, valid prior doses, catch-up intervals, contraindications, vaccine storage/documentation, and access barriers.
sourceStatus: Draft for clinician and governance review

title: Adult Vaccination Review
caseScenario: A 64-year-old with diabetes, chronic lung disease, and planned travel asks which vaccines they need; records are scattered and they are unsure about a previous reaction. The learner must reconcile history and use current Saudi eligibility guidance.
learningFocus: Age, comorbidity, occupation, pregnancy/immunosuppression, travel, prior doses, product availability, and shared decision-making.
sourceStatus: Draft for clinician and governance review

title: Breast Cancer Screening Discussion
caseScenario: A 47-year-old at average apparent risk asks about mammography after a relative’s diagnosis. The learner must clarify personal and family risk, discuss benefits and harms in context of the Saudi programme, and agree an informed plan rather than order screening reflexively.
learningFocus: Risk category, age and life expectancy, family/genetic history, prior breast disease, screening interval, false positives, overdiagnosis, and patient preference.
sourceStatus: Draft for clinician and governance review

title: Cervical Cancer Screening and Follow-Up
caseScenario: A 32-year-old asks for cervical screening, is unsure of prior results, and may be pregnant. The learner must establish eligibility and history, explain HPV-based prevention, use the locally adopted pathway, and ensure abnormal results are followed to resolution.
learningFocus: Age and prior screening, immunosuppression, symptoms, pregnancy, vaccination, screening interval, abnormal-result risk, and closed-loop follow-up.
sourceStatus: Draft for clinician and governance review

title: Colorectal Cancer Screening
caseScenario: A 52-year-old with no symptoms asks whether to complete a stool test or colonoscopy; a first-degree relative had colorectal cancer at a young age. The learner must distinguish average from increased risk and close the loop on abnormal findings.
learningFocus: Symptoms versus screening, family history and hereditary risk, age/health status, test choice, bowel-preparation feasibility, and diagnostic follow-up.
sourceStatus: Draft for clinician and governance review

title: Cardiovascular Risk Assessment
caseScenario: A 46-year-old with tobacco use, elevated blood pressure, and a parent with early myocardial infarction feels well and asks whether treatment is needed. The learner must estimate absolute risk, identify modifiable risks, and agree proportionate prevention.
learningFocus: Absolute versus single-factor risk, age/family history, blood pressure, lipids, diabetes, tobacco, kidney disease, and patient priorities.
sourceStatus: Draft for clinician and governance review

title: Diabetes Screening in At-Risk Adults
caseScenario: A 41-year-old with obesity, prior gestational diabetes, and a strong family history has no symptoms and has not had glucose testing for several years. The learner must confirm screening eligibility, choose an appropriate test, and make a plan for abnormal or borderline results.
learningFocus: Risk-based eligibility, test choice, asymptomatic confirmation, pregnancy history, prediabetes follow-up, and prevention support.
sourceStatus: Draft for clinician and governance review

title: Osteoporosis Risk Assessment and Fracture Prevention
caseScenario: A 67-year-old asks whether she needs bone-density testing after a parent sustained a hip fracture. She has no current fracture symptoms but has several potential risk factors. The learner must assess fracture risk, decide whether testing is appropriate, and discuss prevention and follow-up.
learningFocus: Age and fracture history, secondary causes, falls, medication exposures, bone-density testing, and shared prevention planning.
sourceStatus: Draft for clinician and governance review

title: Tobacco and Nicotine Cessation
caseScenario: A 33-year-old who smokes cigarettes and vapes wants to stop but has relapsed several times and worries about withdrawal. The learner must ask permission, assess dependence and readiness, offer behavioural and pharmacologic options, and plan follow-up without judgement.
learningFocus: Product and use pattern, dependence, prior quit attempts, withdrawal, mental health, pregnancy, household exposure, and accessible support.
sourceStatus: Draft for clinician and governance review

title: Preconception Health and Risk Review
caseScenario: A 29-year-old with diabetes and epilepsy hopes to become pregnant within a year and asks whether she should stop her medicines. The learner must review medical and reproductive history, optimise conditions and medicines safely, and arrange coordinated preconception care.
learningFocus: Pregnancy intentions, chronic disease control, teratogenic medication review, folate and immunisation, genetic/infectious risks, and shared specialist planning.
sourceStatus: Draft for clinician and governance review

title: Elective Hip and Knee Arthroplasty Preparation
caseScenario: A 70-year-old with severe knee osteoarthritis is offered elective replacement after non-operative care has failed. They have obesity, diabetes, and dental concerns. The learner must assess goals and surgical fitness, optimise modifiable risks, and plan shared recovery expectations.
learningFocus: Indication and patient goals, perioperative risk, infection and thrombosis prevention, anaesthetic review, rehabilitation, implant choice, and realistic outcomes.
sourceStatus: Draft for clinician and governance review

title: Cataract Surgery Assessment and Preparation
caseScenario: A 73-year-old reports progressive glare and difficulty reading despite updated glasses; examination suggests cataract. They have diabetes and use anticoagulation. The learner must confirm visual impact, discuss alternatives and expected benefit, and coordinate perioperative planning.
learningFocus: Functional visual impairment, ocular comorbidity, refractive goals, consent/capacity, anaesthetic suitability, and medicine management under local protocol.
sourceStatus: Draft for clinician and governance review

title: Elective Hernia Repair Assessment
caseScenario: A 55-year-old has an enlarging reducible groin bulge that limits work but is not painful at rest. They have obesity and a chronic cough. The learner must confirm hernia type and symptoms, discuss observation versus repair, optimise risks, and plan recovery.
learningFocus: Symptom and reducibility, hernia type, incarceration risk, operative approach, anaesthetic and wound risk, and informed preference.
sourceStatus: Draft for clinician and governance review

title: Colorectal Cancer Diagnosis and Treatment Planning
caseScenario: A 62-year-old has iron-deficiency anaemia and a positive stool test; colonoscopy identifies a lesion. The learner must coordinate histology, staging, multidisciplinary review, patient goals, and timely treatment planning while addressing nutrition and function.
learningFocus: Diagnostic confirmation, anatomical staging, molecular/pathology work-up where indicated, resectability, perioperative fitness, stoma discussion, and MDT coordination.
sourceStatus: Draft for clinician and governance review

title: Prostate Cancer Diagnosis and Treatment Planning
caseScenario: A 68-year-old with rising PSA and urinary symptoms has an MRI lesion and biopsy discussion. The learner must explain uncertainty and overdiagnosis, establish risk category, review life expectancy and preferences, and coordinate urology-oncology decision-making.
learningFocus: Risk stratification, PSA and pathology interpretation, staging, urinary function, competing health risks, active surveillance versus treatment, and patient goals.
sourceStatus: Draft for clinician and governance review

title: Elective Coronary Revascularisation Review
caseScenario: A 64-year-old with stable exertional angina has persistent symptoms despite tolerated medical therapy and coronary imaging showing multivessel disease. The learner must review indication and anatomy with the Heart Team, discuss alternatives and risks, and prepare the patient.
learningFocus: Symptom burden, ischaemic anatomy, ventricular function, diabetes/renal risk, revascularisation modality, antithrombotic planning, and shared decision-making.
sourceStatus: Draft for clinician and governance review

title: Elective Valve Intervention Assessment
caseScenario: A 75-year-old with severe aortic stenosis reports declining exercise tolerance but attributes it to age. Echocardiography confirms progression. The learner must link symptoms to valve severity, assess frailty and procedural options, and coordinate Heart Team review.
learningFocus: Valve lesion and severity, symptoms, ventricular response, pulmonary pressure, frailty, procedural options, timing, and patient goals.
sourceStatus: Draft for clinician and governance review

title: Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery Evaluation
caseScenario: A 42-year-old with severe obesity, obstructive sleep apnoea, and diabetes asks about surgery after structured non-surgical treatment. The learner must assess eligibility under local policy, readiness, comorbidity, nutritional status, and long-term follow-up needs.
learningFocus: Indication and local eligibility, obesity-related disease, psychological/readiness assessment, nutritional deficiency, operative risk, procedure choice, and lifelong follow-up.
sourceStatus: Draft for clinician and governance review

title: Kidney Failure Planning and Dialysis Access
caseScenario: A 59-year-old with progressive CKD is approaching kidney failure and wants to avoid an emergency catheter start. They are uncertain about haemodialysis, peritoneal dialysis, transplantation, and conservative care. The learner must begin shared planning and preserve access options.
learningFocus: Trajectory and kidney failure risk, modality education, transplant eligibility, access timing, vascular preservation, frailty, and patient-defined goals.
sourceStatus: Draft for clinician and governance review

title: Elective Hysterectomy for Benign Disease
caseScenario: A 45-year-old with heavy menstrual bleeding and fibroids has persistent symptoms despite medical treatment and asks about hysterectomy. The learner must clarify diagnosis and fertility goals, review alternatives and risks, and ensure informed consent and perioperative optimisation.
learningFocus: Benign diagnosis confirmation, symptom severity, fertility preference, route and alternatives, anaemia, thrombosis/infection risk, consent and recovery support.
sourceStatus: Draft for clinician and governance review

title: Antenatal Care for Uncomplicated Pregnancy
caseScenario: A 28-year-old at 10 weeks presents for her first antenatal visit. She has no symptoms and a previous uncomplicated birth but is unsure which tests and vaccinations are needed. The learner must establish dating, history, risk, preferences, and a continuity plan using local maternity guidance.
learningFocus: Gestational dating, maternal history and risk, screening and immunisation, nutrition, mental health, safeguarding, birth preferences, and warning signs.
sourceStatus: Draft for clinician and governance review

title: Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy
caseScenario: A 31-year-old at 32 weeks has new elevated blood pressure and a persistent headache; urine testing is abnormal. The learner must assess for severe features and maternal/fetal compromise, distinguish chronic disease from pre-eclampsia, and activate the local obstetric pathway.
learningFocus: Gestational timing, severe features, maternal organ involvement, fetal growth/placental status, seizure/stroke risk, and delivery planning.
sourceStatus: Draft for clinician and governance review

title: Preterm Labour and Threatened Preterm Birth
caseScenario: A 29-year-old at 30 weeks reports regular tightening and pelvic pressure. Membranes appear intact and fetal movement is present. The learner must confirm labour status, assess infection and cervical change, estimate gestational age, and coordinate time-sensitive maternal and neonatal care.
learningFocus: Contraction pattern and cervical change, membrane status, gestational age, infection/bleeding, fetal status, corticosteroid/neuroprotection eligibility, and transfer capability.
sourceStatus: Draft for clinician and governance review

title: Prelabour Rupture of Membranes
caseScenario: A 34-year-old at 35 weeks reports a gush of fluid without contractions. She is afebrile and fetal movement is normal. The learner must confirm membrane rupture, assess gestational age and infection/fetal risks, and plan expectant care or birth under local guidance.
learningFocus: Gestational age, certainty of rupture, latency, infection, fetal presentation/status, Group B streptococcus context, and shared timing of birth.
sourceStatus: Draft for clinician and governance review

title: Postpartum Haemorrhage Response
caseScenario: A 35-year-old has heavy bleeding shortly after vaginal birth with a boggy uterus and dizziness. The learner must call for help, assess haemodynamic compromise, identify the cause, and coordinate immediate multidisciplinary response without delaying resuscitation.
learningFocus: Recognition of blood loss and shock, uterine tone, trauma, retained tissue, coagulopathy, escalation, transfusion, and cause-specific control.
sourceStatus: Draft for clinician and governance review

title: Maternal Sepsis in Pregnancy or Postpartum
caseScenario: A 26-year-old on postpartum day four presents with fever, rigors, abdominal discomfort, and tachycardia. The learner must recognise maternal sepsis, assess organ dysfunction and source, start time-critical local treatment, and coordinate fetal/newborn implications if still pregnant.
learningFocus: Pregnancy-adjusted physiology, infection source, organ dysfunction, cultures and antimicrobial timing, source control, and escalation.
sourceStatus: Draft for clinician and governance review

title: Venous Thromboembolism in Pregnancy and Postpartum
caseScenario: A 33-year-old at 28 weeks develops unilateral leg swelling and pleuritic breathlessness after prolonged immobility. The learner must assess for DVT/PE, choose pregnancy-appropriate diagnostic imaging, and balance anticoagulation, bleeding, delivery, and neuraxial considerations.
learningFocus: Pregnancy-related hypercoagulability, diagnostic test performance, maternal stability, fetal exposure considerations, anticoagulation, and peripartum interruption planning.
sourceStatus: Draft for clinician and governance review

title: Fetal Growth Restriction Assessment
caseScenario: A 30-year-old at 31 weeks has fundal height lag and ultrasound shows estimated fetal weight below expected centile with abnormal placental Doppler. The learner must distinguish constitutionally small fetus from growth restriction and plan surveillance and birth timing.
learningFocus: Growth trajectory, placental function, Doppler and amniotic fluid, maternal disease, fetal wellbeing, gestational age, and neonatal planning.
sourceStatus: Draft for clinician and governance review

title: Reduced Fetal Movements Assessment
caseScenario: A 27-year-old at 34 weeks says the baby has moved much less since yesterday. She has no bleeding or contractions. The learner must take the concern seriously, assess fetal wellbeing promptly, review risk factors, and explain a clear recurrence plan.
learningFocus: Change from the individual fetus’s usual pattern, gestational age, maternal risk, fetal monitoring, growth/placental concern, and recurrence response.
sourceStatus: Draft for clinician and governance review

title: Intrapartum Fetal Compromise
caseScenario: During labour, a 32-year-old’s fetal monitoring shows recurrent decelerations after oxytocin augmentation. The learner must interpret the tracing in context, address reversible contributors, call for senior review, and prepare for expedited birth if compromise persists.
learningFocus: Baseline and variability, deceleration pattern, contraction frequency, maternal position/pressure, oxytocin, labour progress, and response to initial measures.
sourceStatus: Draft for clinician and governance review

title: Cancer Pain Assessment and Support
caseScenario: A 57-year-old with metastatic bone disease reports new pain that interrupts sleep despite prescribed therapy. The learner must characterise pain and function, assess urgent complications, reconcile medicines and preferences, and coordinate safe multimodal relief.
learningFocus: Pain mechanism, severity and function, breakthrough pattern, prior exposure and organ function, adverse effects, bone/nerve complications, and patient preference.
sourceStatus: Draft for clinician and governance review

title: Nausea and Vomiting in Advanced Illness
caseScenario: A 70-year-old with advanced illness has persistent nausea, early satiety, and intermittent vomiting after a recent medication change. They wish to remain at home and avoid burdensome tests. The learner must assess likely causes, hydration, obstruction risk, and a goal-concordant relief plan.
learningFocus: Symptom pattern, medication effects, constipation, metabolic or vestibular causes, obstruction, hydration, route of treatment, and acceptable investigation burden.
sourceStatus: Draft for clinician and governance review

title: Delirium and Agitation Near End of Life
caseScenario: An 82-year-old with advanced cancer becomes inattentive and restless overnight after reduced oral intake and a new medicine. Family fear that the change means imminent death. The learner must assess distress, reversible contributors, safety, capacity, and family communication.
learningFocus: Acute fluctuating attention, potentially reversible causes, medication burden, communication/capacity, distress and safety, and proportionality of investigations.
sourceStatus: Draft for clinician and governance review

title: Advanced Heart Failure Supportive Care
caseScenario: A 76-year-old with repeated heart-failure admissions has persistent breathlessness and fatigue despite specialist therapy. They value time at home and are unsure whether palliative care means stopping cardiology treatment. The learner must clarify goals and treat distress alongside disease-directed care.
learningFocus: Trajectory and uncertainty, symptom burden, treatment burden, device decisions, caregiver support, emergency planning, and concurrent palliative/cardiology input.
sourceStatus: Draft for clinician and governance review

title: Advanced COPD Supportive Care
caseScenario: A 71-year-old with severe COPD remains breathless while dressing despite inhaled treatment and pulmonary rehabilitation. They fear oxygen dependence and have never discussed future crises. The learner must assess reversible contributors, function, goals, and a shared breathlessness plan.
learningFocus: Breathlessness experience and causes, oxygen/ventilation indications, anxiety and deconditioning, exacerbation plan, advance planning, and caregiver support.
sourceStatus: Draft for clinician and governance review

title: Conservative Kidney Care Planning
caseScenario: An 84-year-old with advanced kidney disease, frailty, and cognitive impairment is unlikely to benefit from dialysis on their own terms. The family asks whether declining dialysis means “doing nothing.” The learner must discuss active conservative care, symptoms, values, and support.
learningFocus: Decision-making capacity and surrogate input, expected benefits/burdens of dialysis, symptom management, prognosis uncertainty, advance care planning, and caregiver needs.
sourceStatus: Draft for clinician and governance review

title: Advanced Dementia and Comfort-Focused Care
caseScenario: An 88-year-old with advanced dementia has recurrent aspiration, weight loss, and distress during feeding. Family members disagree about hospital transfer and artificial nutrition. The learner must establish prior wishes, assess reversible illness, and support shared decisions.
learningFocus: Baseline function and prognosis uncertainty, capacity and surrogate role, feeding and aspiration risk, infection treatment goals, comfort, and caregiver support.
sourceStatus: Draft for clinician and governance review

title: Progressive Neurological Disease Support
caseScenario: A 60-year-old with advanced motor neurone disease has worsening communication, swallowing, and breathlessness. They want to remain at home and have not documented preferences about ventilation or emergency transfer. The learner must coordinate specialist, palliative, communication, and caregiver planning.
learningFocus: Disease trajectory and uncertainty, communication capacity, respiratory/nutritional support, symptom burden, device decisions, advance planning, and caregiver resources.
sourceStatus: Draft for clinician and governance review

title: Malignant Bowel Obstruction Support
caseScenario: A 72-year-old with advanced ovarian cancer develops cramping abdominal pain, distension, and repeated vomiting. They prefer symptom relief at home if possible. The learner must assess obstruction and reversible contributors, discuss burdens and benefits of intervention, and create a clear escalation plan.
learningFocus: Complete versus partial obstruction, single versus multiple levels, hydration and symptom burden, prognosis, intervention feasibility, and patient goals.
sourceStatus: Draft for clinician and governance review

title: Last Days of Life Care
caseScenario: A 79-year-old with advanced cancer is bedbound, taking little fluid, and has fluctuating consciousness. Family asks whether they should continue routine medicines and artificial hydration. The learner must recognise possible dying while considering reversible causes, comfort, communication, and family support.
learningFocus: Recognising trajectory with uncertainty, symptom assessment, medication rationalisation, hydration/nutrition choices, cultural/spiritual needs, and family communication.
sourceStatus: Draft for clinician and governance review
